target_customer: Consumers buying discounted gift cards and consumers selling unwanted gift cards
problem: Billions of dollars of gift cards go unused or are given for the wrong store. Cardpool let people sell cards for cash or buy them at a discount.
business_model: Marketplace and inventory buy-and-resell spread on gift cards

founders.name: Tim Wong
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page with no background. TechCrunch (2011) names Anson Tsai instead, so the founder list is not fully consistent.

founders.name: Anson Tsai
previous_startups: Anywhere.com (online music player, acquired by Imeem in 2008)
founders.background_notes: Named by TechCrunch in October 2011 as co-founder; not listed on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Marketplace plus card verification and fraud checks; operations and pricing mattered more than engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Low switching costs for buyers and sellers; advantage came from card inventory, operations and fraud handling.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Blackhawk Network, a Safeway subsidiary selling prepaid cards, acquired Cardpool in October 2011 and kept it as a separate brand in San Francisco.

market_need_then: Unused and unwanted gift cards were common and consumers wanted cash or a discount; the sources opened give no market size figure.

branding.domain_note: Operated at cardpool.com; domain history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Consumer-friendly, savings oriented per product copy

branding.community_and_virality: Used in comparison and coupon-blog coverage (Adweek, review sites) and later charity programs; Better Business Bureau reportedly issued a warning citing complaints, from one search summary.

brand_strength.rationale: Clear descriptive name, kept as a separate brand by Blackhawk after 2011, but review sites cite complaints and no source shows brand driven growth.

outcome_analysis: Cardpool raised angel money from a group including Ron Conway, Max Levchin and Alfred Lin after YC in 2010 and was acquired by Blackhawk Network in October 2011, with terms undisclosed. The quick sale suggests strategic value to a gift card distributor that wanted a secondary-market channel. The team later grew to a reported 251 on the YC page; one aggregator claims the brand shut down in 2021, which is not confirmed.
notes: cardpool.com did not resolve in this session so the site was not checked. Aggregators (CB Insights, Dealroom, Seedtable) report 125K to 150K dollars total raised; recorded as unverified, not as a round amount. Dealroom (single source) says Cardpool ceased operations in early 2021; unverified and conflicts with status Acquired. No dated competitor sources near the 2010 batch were found; later coverage names Plastic Jungle and CardCash but is not dated at founding. Round date 2010 is from an aggregator; the TechCrunch article lists the investors but no date. Success factors are weakly supported.
